Tensor and multitensor categories
Fusion and multifusion categories
Tensor-category terminology follows the EGNO convention
Tensor product in a multitensor category is biexact
items.strategy: Use the left and right duals of a fixed tensor factor to exhibit both adjoints of each tensoring functor; their limit and colimit preservation, together with bilinearity, gives exactness in each variable.

items.title: Dualization in a multitensor category is exact
items.strategy: Use the contravariant duality equivalence to the opposite abelian category and transport short exact sequences through that equivalence, keeping the resulting kernel and cokernel comparison maps canonical.

items.title: Images commute with tensor products in a multitensor category
items.strategy: Factor each morphism through its image, tensor the epi and mono portions one variable at a time using biexactness, and identify the resulting canonical middle object with the image of the tensor product.

items.title: Tensoring with a dualizable object preserves projectives
items.strategy: Transport the relevant Hom functor across the tensor-dual adjunction and compose the projective Hom functor with the exact tensoring functor in the other variable.

items.title: The unit is projective exactly when the tensor category is semisimple
items.strategy: Apply projective preservation to the projective unit to make every object projective, then use the abelian semisimplicity criterion; the converse is immediate.

items.title: The unit object of a multitensor category is semisimple
items.strategy: Follow EGNO's unit-endomorphism and component argument: use image compatibility to obtain the finite indecomposable-unit decomposition, then use exact dualization and a simple subobject to prove that every component unit is simple.

items.title: The unit object of a tensor category is simple
items.strategy: Specialize the semisimple-unit decomposition to the canonical scalar map k to End(1): its being an isomorphism excludes more than one nonzero simple summand.

items.title: Evaluation is epic and coevaluation monic for nonzero objects
items.strategy: Use the simple unit and the two nonzero zig-zag composites: a nonzero map to the simple unit is epic, and a nonzero map from the simple unit is monic.

items.title: Tensor functors between tensor categories
An exact k-linear strong monoidal functor out of a tensor category is faithful
items.strategy: Use monicity of coevaluation to show that an exact strong monoidal functor kills no nonzero object, then apply exactness to the image of a morphism it kills.

items.title: The Grothendieck ring of a tensor category
Grothendieck-ring multiplication is well-defined
items.strategy: Use biexactness to send each short-exact relation to a relation in either tensor variable, so the tensor product descends to the quotient group; the associator and unitors supply the ring laws.

items.title: Fusion rules
Duality induces an anti-involution on the Grothendieck ring
items.strategy: Use exact dualization to descend [X] mapsto [X-vee] through short-exact relations and its antimonoidal structure to reverse products; apply double duality for the square.

items.title: Left and right dual objects are isomorphic in a semisimple multitensor category
items.strategy: Reduce to a simple object and characterize its left and right duals by the unique simple object producing a nonzero unit Hom; semisimplicity equates the two relevant Hom dimensions.

items.title: Objectwise double-dual isomorphisms do not supply a pivotal structure
The boundary of this fusion-category development
Every finite k-linear abelian category is semisimple
items.strategy: Refute the asserted implication by separating the finite and semisimple clauses in the definitions and pointing to the nonsemisimple finite-category phenomenon recorded by the source.

items.title: Every rigid k-linear abelian monoidal category is a tensor category
items.strategy: Compare the assertion with the full tensor-category definition and exhibit the omitted local-finiteness, bilinearity, and scalar-unit hypotheses as independent requirements.

items.title: A tensor functor is just a strong monoidal functor
items.strategy: Compare the general strong-monoidal definition with the tensor-category convention, which also requires k-linearity, exactness, and faithfulness.

items.title: The Grothendieck ring of a tensor category is always commutative
items.strategy: Use the anti-involution formula to identify the available order reversal and explain that a braiding, not tensor-category structure alone, would supply commutativity.

items.title: Objectwise isomorphisms X isomorphic to its double dual supply a pivotal structure
items.strategy: Contrast an objectwise existence statement with the required monoidal natural isomorphism and identify naturality and monoidality as additional coherent data.

items.title: Finite-dimensional vector spaces form a fusion category
items.strategy: Use the published tensor product and dual-basis rigidity of finite-dimensional vector spaces, then verify the finite simple-class and semisimplicity clauses without reconstructing tensor products.

items.title: The Grothendieck ring of finite-dimensional vector spaces
items.strategy: Use the sole simple class [k] and finite direct-sum decompositions to identify the Grothendieck ring with the integers, with multiplication induced by tensor product.

items.title: A matrix multifusion category with nonsimple unit
items.strategy: Construct Mat_n(Vect_fd) from finite matrices of vector spaces, compute its diagonal matrix unit, and exhibit its nontrivial direct-sum decomposition for n greater than one.

items.title: Fusion rules for a supplied finite simple family
items.strategy: Apply the fusion-rule definition to the supplied simple family in finite-dimensional vector spaces and read the unique coefficient from the tensor product of the simple unit with itself.
